clue.text: Intends to make money

explanation.surface: Someone sets out with the plan of getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: He means to go = he intends to go; means are also financial resources, wealth.

clue.text: Pin inserted into a joint

parts.note: reads like carpentry or surgery, but describes the long spike pushed through a joint of meat for roasting

explanation.definitionFit: A long metal or wooden spike thrust through a roast of meat to hold it together while it cooks.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

explanation.surface: Someone talks their way into a place by sheer charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or captivate (stress on the second syllable); also a door or gateway through which one goes inside.

clue.text: Annoyed when out of painkiller?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated to find the medicine cabinet bare of pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ANNOYED; 'when' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a soothing drug that relieves pain, an analgesic.

clue.text: Tips which are never mean

explanation.surface: A remark that gratuities are always generous, never stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but in the second definition it is the statistical average: the farthest points are never the middle value.
explanation.definitionFit: Tips are ends or furthest points; the outermost limits of a range can never be its average.

clue.text: See post go out in March

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the three words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to watch a sentry leave his position at a march past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' at the start of a sentence's end looks like the month; it is the verb, the stiff-legged parade step.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose-step is a straight-legged military way of marching on parade.

clue.text: Considering retribution

explanation.surface: Someone is contemplating revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoning is thinking or calculating; a day of reckoning is when punishment or payback arrives.

clue.text: Once the article for sale is returned, say how good it is

parts.note: ex means former, once so

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for the item at auction is written backwards

parts.note: a lot is an item for sale at an auction

explanation.surface: After an item bought is brought back to the shop, the customer praises it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is returned' turns LOT into TOL, which follows EX; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise something highly, singing its virtues.

clue.text: Miss a festive occasion

parts.note: a miss is a young woman, informally a gal

explanation.surface: Someone skips a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb, fail to attend; it is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a celebratory event or special entertainment.

clue.text: Wars need to be justified

indicators.note: read loosely as 'to become', so the letters of the two words before it are made into something new

explanation.surface: A claim that every war requires a justification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' rearranges WARS and NEED. A charge that is answered has been met and so justified.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge or criticism that has been met with a satisfactory reply is shown to have been rebutted, the conduct vindicated.

clue.text: A vote having gone to the other side

definitions.text: having gone to the other side

parts.note: a voter marks a ballot paper with a cross

explanation.surface: A ballot cast by someone who has defected to the opposing party.
explanation.walkthrough: In British elections you vote by marking a cross beside a candidate's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be across is to have passed over to the far side.

clue.text: Club used in the evening

explanation.surface: A golf club brought out after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not the time of day but making even: the household iron smooths out creases.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with a metal head; also the household appliance pressed over clothes to make them flat and smooth.

clue.text: Mean error puts it just off target

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy, mean with money
a miss is a failure or mistake

explanation.surface: A small slip-up leaves a shot narrowly wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot or strike that narrowly fails to hit its mark; also a narrowly avoided collision.

clue.text: For such an accident, call bronzed doctor, one from overseas

parts.note: hi is a greeting called out to someone
tanned skin is bronzed, so tan
un is French for one

explanation.surface: After a crash, someone summons a suntanned foreign physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word; a hit-and-run accident is one where the driver flees.
explanation.definitionFit: A road collision in which the driver who struck someone leaves without stopping.

clue.text: Tower encountered round about Iran

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the word for met goes outside the other piece

parts.note: to have met someone is to have encountered them

indicators.note: about here means turned around and jumbled, so the letters of the country are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tall tower seen on a tour through Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges IRAN to INAR, which 'round' puts inside MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.

clue.text: Blown to bits, a cat dies in agony

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: in agony suggests writhing and twisting, so the letters of the word before it are contorted

explanation.surface: A pet cat is killed in a violent explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in agony' rearranges DIES to ISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomised means reduced to minute particles, shattered into tiny fragments.

clue.text: Greek hero, oddly sly in habits

indicators.note: in places the anagram inside the word for habits

parts.note: uses are customs or habits

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of the word beside it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hero of Greek legend wears clothes that look a bit shifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for odd letters; it rearranges SLY to LYS, which 'in' puts inside USES. 'habits' looks like clothing; it means customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses is the Latin name of Odysseus, the cunning Greek warrior of the Trojan War.

clue.text: A number making a living in education

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
earning is making money to live on

explanation.surface: Someone works for a wage in the teaching profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is often a Roman numeral in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge gained by study, scholarship.

clue.text: Evidence of a leak? Tell the attendant!

parts.note: to tell can mean to discern or see, as in 'I can tell he is ill'
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: Someone spots a drip and calls for a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'See, page!' as a command to a servant; the letters are SEE and PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly escaping through a crack, which shows there is a leak.

clue.text: What many a simpleton may do when courting

definitions.text: What many a simpleton may do when courting

parts.words: What many a simpleton may do when courting
parts.note: a noodle is a simpleton, and a noodle 'can noodle': the dimwitted lover's ability doubles as the word for kissing and cuddling

explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, as courting couples do.

clue.text: Tied and pulled a bow string

explanation.surface: An archer's contest ended level after he tugged the string back.
explanation.definitionFit: A match drawn is one that ends level; an archer draws the bowstring back before releasing.

clue.text: New labs make good investments

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of the word beside it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh laboratories are a wise financial bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LABS; 'make good' is a link. As printed the clue reads 'investments', which should be 'vestments'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albs are long white linen robes worn by priests at Mass, a kind of clerical garment.

clue.text: Lawyers open with argument that carries weight

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Counsel begin with a weighty submission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open with' is a link: BAR comes first. A barrow is a cart for carrying loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a small wheeled cart pushed by hand to transport heavy loads.

clue.text: Spruce up public transport

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A call to improve the bus and train system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce up' looks like one phrase; 'up' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means neat and trim in appearance, well turned out.

clue.text: Honour I dream about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters of the two words beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of being decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I DREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to hold them in high esteem, to look up to them.

clue.text: Prospect for gold in American state

indicators.note: in places the heraldic gold inside the country name

parts.note: Panama is a state, a nation, in Central America
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Panning for gold somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' looks like a verb, to search for gold; it is a view. 'state' means nation, not one of the US states. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view, a vista.

clue.text: In Australia, football is supreme, O.K.?

explanation.surface: A fan boasts that Aussie football reigns supreme.
explanation.walkthrough: Australian Rules is the Australian code of football; 'X rules OK' is British graffiti declaring X the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian Rules is the national football code down under; something that reigns or dominates is top dog.

clue.text: Battle to get a gangleader on trial

parts.note: the leader of gang is its first letter, G
someone on trial is in court

explanation.surface: A mob boss is brought before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Agincourt is the 1415 battle where Henry V of England defeated the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt is a famous 1415 English victory over the French in the Hundred Years' War.
